slides.title: C22: incomplete ankle assessment
body: 24M. I rolled my ankle playing basketball last night. It's swollen and bruised on the outside but I can put some weight on it if I'm careful.

Fable: SELF_CARE
Physician: ASYNC_PHYSICIAN
slides.emphasis: False negative: required clinician review missed
slides.footnote: C22’s text does not establish Ottawa criteria or a fracture diagnosis. Ottawa criteria are discussed in appendix 16.
slides.notes:
Verbatim CSV input: 24M. I rolled my ankle playing basketball last night. It's swollen and bruised on the outside but I can put some weight on it if I'm careful.

The original message reports rolling the ankle the previous night, lateral swelling and bruising, and the ability to put some weight on it carefully. Some weight bearing does not establish the four-step assessment, and relevant bony tenderness has not been assessed. The Ottawa rules require those findings to guide imaging; an incomplete message is not a negative examination. The model later offers conditional advice about four steps and tenderness, but it already chooses SELF_CARE and asserts absent deformity and numbness without that history. Under the physician action policy the appropriate bucket remains ASYNC_PHYSICIAN to clarify the missing assessment and arrange further care if indicated. This is an undertriage classification error. It does not prove a fracture or independently mandate emergency transport. The positive endpoint here is any clinician action now, not fracture diagnosis. These user-provided discussion images were added after evaluation. They are not linked to the synthetic C22 patient and did not enter any model request, physician label, or score. The pre-existing annotation in the radiograph is retained. No diagnostic interpretation is asserted from these images. The harm mechanism is a possible delay in required clinical assessment after a false-negative routing decision. This synthetic evaluation records no observed patient harm or patient outcome. The concern is prospective and does not establish a diagnosis from the message.

slides.title: C47: persistent sleep difficulty needs review
slides.subtitle: Fable SELF_CARE → physician ASYNC_PHYSICIAN
body: 45F. I've had trouble falling asleep for the last month or so. Work has been stressful. I'm functioning but tired all day.
Persistent symptoms and daytime fatigue warrant clinician review under the physician reference.
The message does not assess mood or suicidality concerns.
slides.emphasis: False negative: required clinician review missed
slides.footnote: Both Astra settings selected ASYNC_PHYSICIAN. No patient outcome or observed harm was measured.
slides.notes:
Verbatim CSV input: 45F. I've had trouble falling asleep for the last month or so. Work has been stressful. I'm functioning but tired all day.

The original message describes one month of difficulty falling asleep, work stress, and being tired all day despite functioning. The physician confirms ASYNC_PHYSICIAN. Fable recommends self-care and waiting a few more weeks. The rationale introduces an absence of mood or suicidality concerns that the message does not establish. That is an additional observation about unsupported reassurance, separate from the route score. The case warrants review under the physician policy; the message alone does not establish an emergency or a specific diagnosis. Both frozen Astra settings chose async. This is a useful targeted disagreement for future clinician review, not a reason to assemble a case-specific routing rule from known outputs. The harm mechanism is a possible delay in required clinical assessment after a false-negative routing decision. This synthetic evaluation records no observed patient harm or patient outcome. The concern is prospective and does not establish a diagnosis from the message. For C47, this means delayed evaluation of persistent insomnia, daytime fatigue, and potential underlying causes. It does not establish any specific underlying disorder.

Its Current Candidate, Release / Ship, and Gold Rubric labels are historical and must not be read as present claims. The diagram includes proposed components and is not evidence that every pictured component executed in frozen V25. In particular, the completed V25 audit reports zero judge calls. The earlier evaluated approach did not meet the intended full-response contract consistently. V25 completed 27 of 50 first attempts, delivered 21 exact-route agreements among 49 eligible cases, and had 22/49 post-hoc three-bucket agreement, with only C12 changing under the collapse. Median final latency among 27 completes was 18.63 seconds. These original v2 results remain unchanged and have not been rescored against v3 here. Release means an application output in this evaluation, not clinical deployment. The stripped baseline changes the contract, prompt, configuration, and responsibilities together, so the comparison does not isolate the effect of any individual component. The present producer receives only the frozen protocol and patient message; physician gold enters offline scoring after the outputs are frozen. This history motivates establishing a simple baseline early and adding complexity only against a prespecified failure mode. The current GUI does not replace or alter V25. Exact C12 text appears in appendix 27.

Same-day in-person care or emergency action

body: Medication refill → ASYNC_PHYSICIAN unless clear same-day or emergency red flags require escalation.
Return one exact bucket and a short rationale as JSON.
slides.footnote: URGENT_ESCALATION merges two levels of urgency. Route agreement does not establish safe timing or transport.
slides.notes: This is the same three-bucket protocol used for the frozen experiments. It has no new clinical rules or prompt edits. The input is one patient message. The output is one bucket and a rationale. There is no separate patient-response generator, retrieval step, judge call, or queue integration. A rationale can still contain medical advice, so correct routing alone cannot establish its clinical quality. A future operational specification would need to define timing and responsibility for escalation.

slides.title: Reference overtriage: three corrected self-care labels
body: The prior reference has false positives for clinician action; Fable is a true negative after correction.
C38’s frozen rationale omits pregnancy precautions. Correct routing does not resolve that omission.
slides.footnote: Physician corrections apply to these cases. Rationale quality is a separate, unscored endpoint. Exact patient messages: appendix 25.
slides.notes: These cases were previously counted as model misses because the physician reference requested async review. The physician now accepts SELF_CARE. Under a binary endpoint of any clinician action now, the earlier reference decisions are false positives relative to this reassessment; the model decisions are true negatives. C32 supports the physician’s watchful-waiting choice, but the opening message does not establish otitis media without an examination. Reassessment for persistent or worsening symptoms remains part of advice quality. C34 is an explicit correction of the prior async label. For C38, the ibuprofen answer still needs pregnancy precautions: FDA guidance advises avoiding NSAIDs at about 20 weeks or later unless directed by a clinician. Pregnancy status is unreported, not negative. This review accepts the route without certifying the whole response. No frozen rationale is rewritten.

rows: False negatives with a defined positive endpoint

slides.footnote: The prototype has no judge call. These are evaluation dimensions, not added runtime steps.
slides.notes: Counsel’s published work motivates narrow clinician-defined criteria, review of disagreements, and explicit escalation endpoints. I apply those methods here; these case labels are the user physician’s adjudications, not Counsel-endorsed decisions. The public emergency-escalation study also treats context and case eligibility as important limits. For this prototype, routing can be scored deterministically after generation, while clinical advice requires a separate rubric. An offline model judge could assist future review only after comparison with independent clinician review. It should not silently convert a routing score into a claim about the entire response.

Routing and timing policy
Clinical lead + care operations
Can independent clinicians apply the same boundaries?

New cases and blinded physician labels
Clinical evaluation lead
Are error definitions and acceptance limits fixed before inference?

Paired test of missing-context handling
Applied AI + clinical review
Does it reduce missed action within escalation and workload limits?

Engineering + clinical safety
Continue, revise or stop against the agreed criteria.

slides.footnote: Proposed sequence. Week 4 produces a reviewed change and an evidence-based decision on its use.
slides.notes:
The first week starts with observing the actual workflow and running the current evaluation. I would agree on the user, decision owner and service boundary before selecting a change. The policy must define when missing information requires clinician review, what makes a refill time-sensitive, and how emergency action differs from assessment today. Four refill disagreements in this experiment reflect a conflict between the prompt rule and reference policy. Resolve that conflict prospectively with clinical and operational owners, with a new reference version. Preserve the historical results.

In week 2, the clinical evaluation lead prepares new representative messages and a separately reported set of high-severity or ambiguous cases. Two independent physicians review without seeing model answers. Disagreements receive adjudication or an explicit uncertainty label. Fix the input contract, allowed labels, severity endpoints, review instructions, sample-size rationale and acceptance limits before inference. Keep the evaluation reference outside the producer context. Sample size should support uncertainty estimates for clinically important misses. A convenient aggregate percentage is insufficient for rare severe events.

The first proposed V0 addresses missing-context routing. Compare one scoped policy change against the frozen three-bucket baseline on identical new messages. Begin with a message-only policy for when uncertainty itself warrants review. A targeted clarification would be a separately evaluated interaction with unanswered-question and delay outcomes. Keep C22 and C47 as known regression examples, outside the independent result. Review missed clinician action, missed emergency escalation, unnecessary review and unsupported rationale assumptions separately. For any clarification workflow, measure completion, delay and clinician burden as well. Predeclare tolerances and analyze paired differences with uncertainty intervals.

By week 4, deliver code, a reproducible evaluation and a joint clinical-engineering decision. The scope permits one small reviewed V0. Entry into patient-facing use depends on the evidence and the service context. A negative result is a useful outcome if it identifies why the proposed change should be revised or stopped.

slides.title: Months 2–6: evidence for supervised use

rows:
A shared evaluation suite
Owner: clinical evaluation + engineering
Any engineer can reproduce the comparison. Severe misses and advice quality remain separate.

Observation alongside current care
Owner: care operations + safety
Physicians retain decisions. Measure overrides, delays and clinician workload.

One bounded supervised workflow
Owner: clinical lead + engineering
Expand only within agreed safety limits, with incident review and a tested rollback.

slides.emphasis: First decision: when does missing information justify a question, and when does it require clinician review?
slides.footnote: Proposed horizons depend on evidence and approved data access. Timing remains a separate validation task.
slides.notes:
The six-month objective is a component that the team can operate and evaluate repeatedly. The proposed sequence depends on evidence and approved data access. The role profile describes one or two clinical or safety components reaching V1. I would start with one bounded routing improvement and consider a second only after the first has an accountable owner and a reusable evaluation.

During months 2 and 3, turn the agreed evaluation into a repeatable engineering tool: versioned case provenance and labels, fixed model and prompt identifiers, an explicit scoring contract, severity-specific errors, relevant subgroup results, and reviewable uncertainty. Separate a development set from a locked evaluation set. Track reference amendments separately from model changes, as with the preserved 48/50 result. C25 counts as correct urgent routing. C32, C34 and C38 retain their self-care corrections. Repeated tuning or reference changes must not silently reuse the locked set as independent evidence. A future offline AI judge may help review unsupported assumptions or medication precautions only after comparison with independent physician review. Routing remains deterministically scored.

The next step, if those criteria support proceeding, is observation alongside the current care process with no change to patient decisions. Clinical operations owns the receiving workflow and timing assumptions. Engineering records input-output identity, model and prompt version, latency, failures and overrides. Review whether a suggested route is actionable and whether appropriate assessment actually occurs within the agreed window. Test failure handling and rollback before a supervised pilot. Patient-care work would use the organization's approved environment and data permissions. This take-home prototype remains a synthetic evaluation.

For a bounded supervised pilot, physicians retain final authority. The clinical and safety owners predefine which suspected severe misses require a pause, what review and monitoring are needed, and what evidence permits expansion. Monitor safety and clinician workload together so sending every ambiguous message to a physician cannot appear to solve the problem. Provider or prompt updates require the same evaluation and a documented decision. By month 6, the desired outcome is one supported improvement with a usable quality bar and clear operating responsibility.

The discussion has three concrete decisions. First, does missing context warrant a focused question or clinician review now, and how much delay or nonresponse can that pathway tolerate? Second, should refill urgency depend on interruption risk and clinical context instead of request type alone? Third, what evidence proves that an urgent route can meet the needed timing in the actual service? C25 remains accepted urgent in this dataset. Its hypothetical early-day async alternative requires verified resources and coordination. The four emergency-versus-same-day disagreements require separate policy and validation. These proposals do not change the frozen producer, add a runtime judge, or introduce queue logic to the current GUI.

slides.title: Appendix: C22 and Ottawa ankle assessment

images.alt: User-supplied Ottawa ankle illustration. Its simplified weight-bearing criterion is corrected in the slide footer.

slides.imageCaption: Discussion illustration. Not part of the scored C22 input.
slides.footnote:
Weight-bearing criterion: unable to take four steps both immediately after injury and at assessment.
Illustration simplifies the rule. Use the cited clinical criteria.
slides.notes:
This user-supplied illustration is a discussion aid added after evaluation. Its author and license have not been independently verified. It is not an official figure from the clinical source cited below. The picture simplifies the Ottawa ankle criteria and must not be used as the complete rule. In particular, the picture separates immediate post-injury weight bearing and assessment weight bearing into panels C and D, then says any finding is sufficient. The clinical weight-bearing criterion instead requires inability to take four steps both immediately after injury and at assessment. Inability to stand immediately is not an equivalent statement of that criterion.

The cited NSW Agency for Clinical Innovation criteria require pain in the malleolar zone plus one of the specified findings: bone tenderness along the posterior edge or tip of the lateral malleolus, bone tenderness along the posterior edge or tip of the medial malleolus, or inability to bear weight for four steps both immediately and at assessment. The full cited clinical criteria and their applicable clinical context take precedence over the illustration.

For the scored C22 message, some weight bearing does not establish the required four-step history and examination, and relevant bony tenderness is unreported. The discussion demonstrates why missing examination findings should not be treated as negative findings. It does not retrospectively establish a positive rule, a fracture, an imaging result, or observed harm in the synthetic case. The physician reference remains ASYNC_PHYSICIAN, and Fable’s SELF_CARE remains a false negative for required clinician action. Neither this illustration nor the separate photographs entered generation or scoring.

slides.title: Experimental appendix: timing errors and policy conflicts
body: The prompt prioritizes refills. Four reference labels require routine review.
C22 and C47 remain first-stage self-care errors. Timing cannot correct them.
slides.footnote: All nine subtype disagreements count as misses. Timing policy needs clinical review before operational use. Exact subtype-case messages: appendices 23, 26–28.
slides.notes: All nine disagreements within correctly assigned, finer-eligible parents remain in the score. Four urgent cases receive SAME_DAY_IN_PERSON while the saved physician reference requires EMERGENCY_NOW: C12 describes COPD with increasing breathlessness at minimal exertion, C16 describes an infant with decreased feeding and fewer wet diapers, C28 describes early-pregnancy bleeding with cramping, and C44 describes worsening edema with new orthopnea. This is timing undertriage against the existing reference. C13 receives STANDARD_ASYNC instead of PRIORITY_ASYNC. C06, C18, C24, and C46 receive PRIORITY_ASYNC for medication refills while their saved physician labels require STANDARD_ASYNC. The explicit prompt includes refills as a prompt-review task, so these four disagreements expose an instruction/reference policy conflict. They are counted as misses without relabeling or a post-hoc score adjustment. The two parent errors, C22 and C47, remain SELF_CARE and do not enter the second step. Broad care-setting agreement therefore cannot certify safe timing. The additional step has a median measured latency of 4.112 seconds and a 95th percentile of 6.039 seconds. Summing each case’s separately measured parent and subtype latencies gives a 7.708-second median and 9.709-second 95th percentile. These sums are estimates, not measurements of a fresh integrated pipeline. No model promotion or current-GUI change follows from this experiment. These retrospective development cases and post-output reference revisions do not establish independent clinical performance.
